title: Compatible finite local bases for a normalized reduction tower
statement: Let l be prime, E a finite extension of Q_l, and X any scheme. Use the integral coefficient sheaf and normalized positive reduction towers of [def-per-integral-lisse-reduction-data]. Every such tower F has a family U_i of pro-etale objects covering the terminal sheaf and finite types kappa_i, such that restriction of F to the slice over U_i is naturally isomorphic, as a whole inverse diagram of integral module sheaves, to the scalar-cokernel tower of the integral free sheaf on kappa_i, restricted to that slice. The cover is allowed to be empty on the empty base and ranks may be zero or vary between members.

source.place: Lemma 6.8.2(1),(2), Definition 6.8.3, Proposition 6.8.4(1), p. 59; the reduction ring identification is the rank-one reduction in this proposition.

proof.text:
Proof: trivialize the first level and refine the covering to weakly contractible affines.
Transitions are scalar cokernel projections, hence epic, and their section maps on these
objects are surjective by exactness of evaluation. Lift the first basis successively and
use the free-module universal property to obtain compatible integral free-module maps.
The scalar annihilates each target level, so these maps descend through the preserved
scalar cokernels on the slice. Induct on the level to prove the descended maps invertible.
On weakly contractible refinements of a chart of the next level, evaluation gives an exact
scalar-cokernel presentation by a projective finite free integral module. Lift the previous
inverse from this projective presentation, and descend it since the larger scalar kills
the source quotient. Both inverse errors vanish after reduction. Exactness and commutation
with the smaller scalar imply their squares vanish, since that scalar has square zero.
Correcting by one minus the error gives a two-sided inverse. Isomorphisms are detected
on these covering refinements. Adjacent compatibility then gives a natural isomorphism
of the whole diagrams. Zero and varying ranks and empty objects require no extra assumption.

The weakly contractible refinements and their affine construction are the already proved Scheme.ProEt.exists_isWeaklyContractible_cover in WeilConjectures.AlgebraicGeometry.ProEtale.WeaklyContractible. Evaluation is exact by a direct proof: the forgetful functor preserves epimorphisms, these are locally surjective on underlying sets, and weak contractibility makes them surjective on sections. Additivity and preservation of kernels then give finite-colimit preservation. The finite evaluated free integral module is projective since evaluation preserves finite coproducts and the evaluated unit is the coefficient ring itself. The private square-zero correction lemma is proved directly in the abelian category; no matrix-lifting theorem or rank-comparison lemma is assumed.

proof_origin.place: Proposition 6.8.4(1), omitted proof supplied by compatible sections, scalar cokernel descent and projective square-zero inverse lifting; weakly contractible refinements use the proved upstream source.

lean.statement:
theorem integralLisseTower_localBases (F : IntegralReductionTower l E X) :
    ∃ (I : Type (u + 1)) (U : I → X.ProEt) (κ : I → Type (u + 1)),
      (Scheme.ProEt.topology X).CoversTop U ∧ (∀ i, Finite (κ i)) ∧
      ∀ i, Nonempty (F.obj ⋙ SheafOfModules.overFunctor (integralLisseRing l E X) (U i) ≅
        integralLisseCokernelTower l E X
          (SheafOfModules.free (R := integralLisseRing l E X) (κ i)) ⋙
            SheafOfModules.overFunctor (integralLisseRing l E X) (U i))
